question.prompt: A radio program has a quiz consisting of \(3\) multiple-choice questions, each with \(3\) choices. A contestant wins if he or she gets \(2\) or more of the questions right. The contestant answers randomly to each question. What is the probability of winning?

solutions.title: Count two or three correct
solutions.explanation:
Winning means getting either exactly two questions right or all three right. These cases cannot overlap.

Each independent random answer has probability \(1/3\) of being right and \(2/3\) of being wrong. Thus the probability of all three being right is
\[
\left(\frac13\right)^3=\frac1{27}.
\]
For exactly two right answers, the missed question can be the first, second, or third. Each of these three disjoint patterns has probability \((1/3)^2(2/3)\), so
\[
P(\text{exactly two right})=3\left(\frac13\right)^2\left(\frac23\right)=\frac6{27}.
\]
Adding the two winning cases gives
\[
P(\text{win})=\frac1{27}+\frac6{27}=\boxed{\frac7{27}},
\]
choice (D).
